blacklistabilityReview.evidence: At Ethereum block 26095800 (2026-10-01), canonical GHO bytecode matched the verified GhoToken and ordinary ERC-20 implementation; the EIP-1967 implementation and correct admin slots were zero. Its transfer paths contain no holder blacklist, freeze, seizure or global pause, and the external burn function burns only the caller's balance. The current Chainlink directory identifies the nine non-Ethereum deployments as BurnMint pools. The prior inherited-status rationale cited obsolete 44.3% mainnet GSM and 7.4% stataUSDT weights. The September 30 reserve review instead records 41.630945892818% unresolved mainnet GSM residual, 2.718124202359% measured stataUSDT and positive USDC dust, plus unresolved remote allocations. Unknown residual issuance is not proof of specific issuer holdings. The adverse inherited verdict is retained pending reconciliation of the opaque exposures and owner review of the greater-than-50% test; no current threshold-satisfaction claim is made.

oracleRisk.summary: Ethereum Core, Lido and Horizon are price-sensitive lending paths. Exact Mainnet/Plasma/Arbitrum/Monad GhoDirectFacilitator allocations have no local price or liquidation authority at Ethereum block 26098749, independently confirmed at block 26098867; this does not classify remote GSM collateral or downstream pricing. OWNER-2026-10-01-horizon-nav admits Horizon's Chainlink-relayed administrator NAV feeds as standard-external with documented underlying feed heartbeats; timestamp enforcement, permissioned RWA liquidation and absent local Umbrella remain distinct limitations.

collateralParameters.note: Aave Governance configures reserve-specific LTV, liquidation threshold, and liquidation bonus parameters; the account health factor applies the value-weighted liquidation thresholds across supplied collateral.

branches.liquidationMechanism: When account health factor falls below 1, any participant may repay GHO debt and receive priced collateral plus the reserve liquidation bonus; current V3 logic permits 50% or 100% close factors based on health factor and position size.
branches.backstop: Aave Umbrella provides asset-specific automated deficit coverage for Ethereum Core, including a GHO module that can burn staked GHO to cover a realized GHO reserve deficit after the configured deficit offset.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: Aave V3.3 checks for zero collateral with remaining debt after liquidation, burns the remaining variable GHO debt, and records the amount as a GHO reserve deficit that can subsequently be covered through Umbrella; the reviewed sources do not describe a global GHO shutdown path.

branches.liquidationMechanism: Aave liquidationCall repays debt and releases priced RWA collateral when health-factor and reserve checks permit. Liquidators must meet RWA issuer transfer/investor requirements; this is not unrestricted liquidation or guaranteed atomic redemption. At Ethereum block 26100093 (timestamp 1790889335), getLiquidationGracePeriod returned 0 for all eight listed RWA collateral assets and GHO debt; no grace was active. The pinned Pool implementation's LiquidationLogic and ValidationLogic impose no other time delay; the provider's priceOracleSentinel was address(0). Reserve pause and issuer eligibility checks remain applicable, not a fixed delay.
branches.backstop: The Horizon provider UMBRELLA entry is address(0) at block 26098749; Core stkGHO covers only the Core Pool and supplies no automatic Horizon deficit backstop.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: Deployed LiquidationLogic burns residual debt after collateral exhaustion and records reserve deficit. No local automatic Umbrella is registered. Issuer-token permissions and reserve pause/grace settings can constrain liquidation; no global GHO shutdown is established.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: GHO is natively issued on Ethereum by Aave facilitators; its cross-chain destination deployments are minted via Chainlink CCIP burn/mint pools, with the Ethereum CCIP pool acting as lock/release for supply in transit. The CCIP common-mode failure domain applies to the bridged destination routes; the natively held Ethereum supply is not CCIP-dependent. The route is external validated-network infrastructure governed by Aave/CCIP controls.
bridgeRouteRisk.reviewer: Codex AB-CURATION bridge re-review (native-route common-mode attribution)

routes.reviewNote: Canonical GHO is natively issued on Ethereum by Aave GHO facilitators (native-mint); the natively held Ethereum supply does not depend on Chainlink CCIP. The Ethereum CCIP lock/release pool only governs GHO that is actively moving to or from burn/mint destination deployments, so the CCIP common-mode domain is attributed to the cross-chain destination routes rather than to the native home supply.
